items.title: 655th ISRW current squadron lay-down
items.note: The squadron breakdown originally rested on a 2018 fact sheet. Units reorganize — flagged high priority because the 14th IS acquisition-intelligence mission is a load-bearing claim on this map.
items.finding: RESOLVED, WITH A CORRECTION. The official page confirms the 14th IS (acquisitions — intelligence supportability, materiel lifecycle, partnered with AFLCMC’s 21st IS) and the 64th IS (HUMINT — directly supports NASIC’s Global Exploitation Group) at WPAFB. But the 71st IS is now at FORT MEADE, MD, not WPAFB as the 2018 sheet implied; it supports NASIC’s Geospatial & Signatures Intelligence Group from there. The 655th ISRG now lists seven squadrons, not three. Wing: 1,100+ personnel, 10th AF, two groups, 14 squadrons, seven states. Dashboard corrected.

items.title: KBR–Macaulay-Brown acquisition
items.tag: MAP REF C-03 · DASHBOARD ERROR FOUND
items.query: SEC filings (HII 8-K and FY2021 10-K), Veritas Capital release, Washington Technology, KippsDeSanto deal announcement.
items.note: The dashboard claimed KBR acquired Dayton’s Macaulay-Brown ("MacB") in 2018, graded [V].
items.finding: RESOLVED — THE CLAIM WAS FALSE. MacB was acquired by ALION SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (a Veritas Capital portfolio company) in Aug 2018. Alion was then acquired by HUNTINGTON INGALLS INDUSTRIES for $1.65B, closing 19 Aug 2021, into HII’s Technical Solutions division. KBR was never part of that chain. KBR Wyle remains a legitimate NASIC A&AS IDIQ awardee — that part stands. The MacB lineage claim has been removed and replaced with the corrected chain. This is exactly what the queue is for.

items.title: 123rd Air Control Squadron current status
items.query: nationalguard.mil, ang.af.mil, DVIDS, Blue Ash ANGS pages.
items.note: The unit was carried as unverified [V]; a C2 mission, treated as a geographic fallback only.
items.finding: RESOLVED, AND MORE USEFUL THAN EXPECTED. The 123rd ACS is active (about 300 Airmen returned from deployment Dec 2025), at Blue Ash ANGS since 1953, and provides worldwide command, control, and communications. Critically: multiple Air Force and National Guard releases describe it as "the 178th Wing’s 123rd Air Control Squadron." The wing whose ISR group supports NASIC also fields a squadron ~15 mi from downtown Cincinnati. Mission is C2, not intelligence — geographic reach, not an analytic node.

items.title: AFRL information/cyber directorate location
items.query: AFRL/RI pages, AFRL Summer Faculty Fellowship lab listing, CNY Defense Alliance, Rome Research Site visitor documents.
items.note: The dashboard assumes the crypto-relevant AFRL customer is centered on Rome, NY, not WPAFB. If wrong, SBIR targeting guidance changes materially.
items.finding: RESOLVED — ASSUMPTION CONFIRMED. AFRL’s Information Directorate (AFRL/RI) is at the Rome Research Site, 525 Brooks Rd, Rome, NY, employing 700+ civilian scientists and engineers across C4I and cyber S&T. Not resident at WPAFB. Bonus: AFRL/RI publishes research topics on secure, scalable Publicly Available Information (PAI) collection that protects analyst identity and intent.

items.title: DoD-specific crypto-analytics contract awards
items.tag: NO MAP NODE · CENTRAL ANALYTIC QUESTION · FINDING CORRECTED
items.query: USASpending.gov API (spending_by_award), run 2026-11-10: recipient search “Chainalysis”, “TRM Labs”, “Elliptic” · awarding agency Department of Defense (toptier) · contracts (A–D) and IDVs · FY2008 → 2026-11-10; then each award’s detail record for office, funding office and place of performance. Same search across all agencies as a control.
items.note: Distinguishes confirmed DoD purchases from the well-documented Treasury/DOJ/DHS buys already on file.
items.finding: RESOLVED — DoD HAS BOUGHT CRYPTO ANALYTICS, BUT NOT IN DAYTON. The earlier “no DoD award found” was wrong. USASpending lists six DoD contracts to the three vendors, $7,677,380 obligated, every one awarded by Air Force contracting: Chainalysis ×4 (FA714618M0419, $110,500, 2018; FA714620P0919, $799,740, 2020; FA714622PB004, $2,266,375, 2022; FA481422P0038, $6,250, 2022, funded by HQ USSOCOM J3), Elliptic ×1 (FA714624C0017, $3,494,525, 2024) and TRM Labs ×1 (FA714625P0003, $999,990, 2025). Five were awarded by office “FA7146 SAF OC PK” and one by “FA4814 6 CONS PK”. Places of performance: Tampa, FL (five) and New York, NY (one). None names Dayton, WPAFB or an Ohio place of performance, so the map’s position holds: the region is not a documented crypto-analytics buyer. No DoD IDVs to any of the three. For scale, civilian buys dwarf these: the same search across all agencies returns 100+ Chainalysis contracts (largest $26.8M, IRS) and TRM’s $94.7M ICE contract (2026). One DoD hit was a name collision (“Elliptical Surveys Inc”, Army, 2007) and is excluded.
